investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods stuck unscheduled for ~144–147 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Simultaneously, the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements, leaving 0 of 6 nodes schedulable. Because preemption found no victims on the 2 kata nodes and is not applicable on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes, every new remote-agent pod is permanently blocked at scheduling. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never receives a running VM, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is written and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 256) is entirely unmet.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other workloads have consumed all allocatable kata peer-pod slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes may have had labels removed or the pod spec's nodeSelector/affinity rules may have been tightened, shrinking the schedulable pool to only the 2 kata nodes that are now full.

Tertiary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or limit set too low for the current workload: the cluster may have a ResourceQuota or node-level device plugin configuration that caps the number of concurrent peer-pod VMs below actual demand.
Quaternary — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: previously created agents that were not cleaned up may be occupying resource slots, preventing new allocations.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods stuck unscheduled for ~144–147 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Simultaneously, the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements, leaving 0 of 6 nodes schedulable. Because preemption found no victims on the 2 kata nodes and is not applicable on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes, every new remote-agent pod is permanently blocked at scheduling. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never receives a running VM, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is written and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 256) is entirely unmet.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=149931, status=fail — a third independent pod submission hit the same resource exhaustion, confirming the condition is cluster-wide and not pod-specific.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: previously created agents that were not cleaned up may be occupying resource slots, preventing new allocations.
